transfer resistor

most abundant element in Earth’s crust.

one impurity atom in 10⁶ to 10⁸ atoms

An amplifier increases the strength of weak signals.
Rectifiers are classified as half-wave or full-wave, and a solar cell converts light to electricity.

a high-Tc cuprate superconductor

is a natural insulator.

atts.

Conductors have very low resistivity.

, glass and plastic have very high resistivity.

Silver is an example of a conductor.

ultraviolet radiation
in semiconductor manufacturing.

range finding, targeting, and directed energy

dioptre
s (D).

vacuum

form images.
Objects in water appear raised because of apparent depth.

decorative illumination and medical illumination

Astigmatism involves different powers in different meridians.

The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction succeeded the Hyogo Framework for Action (HFA) 2005–2015.
The second priority of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction is strengthening disaster risk governance.
Target E sets 2020, not 2030, for increasing the number of countries with national and local DRR strategies.
All-of-society engagement involves government.
The expected outcome of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction is a substantial reduction of disaster risk.
Hazard, vulnerability, exposure and capacity constitute the dimensions in which disaster risk is assessed.
Strengthening disaster risk governance emphasizes laws, institutions, policies and coordination at all levels.
Both public and private investment in prevention and mitigation are emphasized under investing in disaster risk reduction for resilience.
Preparedness, recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction are all emphasized under Priority 4: enhancing disaster preparedness for effective response and to “Build Back Better”.
Target A concerns global disaster mortality, Target B concerns the number of affected people, and Target D covers both damage to critical infrastructure and disruption of basic services by 2030.
Target F is to
substantially enhance international cooperation to developing countries by 2030
States have the primary role in reducing disaster risk.
Build Back Better links recovery with reducing future risk, while the inclusive and people-centred principle specifically gives attention to vulnerable groups.

is the nodal agency for forecasting heatwaves.
A heatwave is a period of abnormally high temperatures exceeding the normal maximum temperature during the summer season.
Heatwave is a notified disaster.
The green colour alert level indicates normal conditions.
The minimum threshold temperatures are 40°C for plains, 37°C for coastal areas and 30°C for hilly regions.
The
NDMA Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan – Prevention and Management of Heat Wave
provide key guidelines for heatwave management.

A plains heatwave and a hilly-region heatwave are declared at a departure of 4.5°C to 6.4°C. A severe plains heatwave requires a departure of more than 6.4°C, while the coastal criterion is 4.5°C or more.
In plains, a heatwave may also be identified when the actual maximum temperature is at least 45°C, while a severe heatwave is identified at at least 47°C.
Heat Action Plans are prepared by
states and cities
with support from NDMA and IMD.
Cool roofs use
reflective coatings or white painting of roofs
Public awareness measures include communicating do’s and don’ts.
Structural measures include shade structures, drinking water points, and adjusted working hours.

For plains based on actual temperature, a cold wave is declared when the actual minimum temperature is 4°C or below.
A cold wave is a significant drop in minimum temperature below the normal climatological average during winter.

For plains, the threshold is 10°C or below; a cold wave has a negative departure of 4.5°C to 6.4°C and a severe cold wave exceeds 6.4°C. For hilly regions, the threshold is 0°C or below, with the same departure ranges for cold and severe cold waves.
A cold day is declared when the maximum temperature departure is –4.5°C to –6.4°C while the minimum temperature is already low.
Cold waves can cause respiratory diseases.
Cold waves affect livestock.

Protective measures against cold waves include medical preparedness.
